spike: SPIKE 2 — per-redirect SSRF validation via a `fetch` override on the MCP client transports

fallback_verified: Not needed (claim CONFIRMED), but I checked reachability anyway: `import('node:undici')` → `ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE`, `import('undici')` → `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Node 22 bundles undici internally but exposes no importable module, so the `Agent({maxRedirections:0})` fallback would require adding `undici` as a real dependency. Don't take it.
impact: None to the spec as written. Two implementation notes worth pinning into §14/ssrf.ts: (1) put the redirect policy inside `guardedFetch`, not in `requestInit` — the StreamableHTTP GET-stream open builds its own init and drops `requestInit` (observed `redirect=(unset)`); (2) apply `redirect:'manual'` *after* spreading the incoming init, since SSE's EventSource passes `redirect:'follow'` (observed `redirect=follow`).
gotchas: `requestInit` is NOT applied to every request. `streamableHttp.js:90` (`_startOrAuthSse`, the GET stream + every reconnect) builds its init literal without spreading `_requestInit` — my recorder printed `redirect=(unset)` for those GETs while POST/DELETE showed `redirect=manual`. Anything security-relevant must live in the fetch function, never in `requestInit`.

SSE's EventSource passes `redirect: 'follow'` in the init it hands your fetch (printed `redirect=follow`). `fetch(url, { redirect:'manual', ...init })` would silently be overwritten back to follow. Spread first, force `redirect` last.

Node's `redirect:'manual'` returns the REAL response, not a browser-style opaqueredirect: `status = 307 | type = basic | location = /r2`. `Location` is readable and `res.status` is the true code — the hop loop is straightforward. (Browser/edge runtimes would give `type: 'opaqueredirect'`, status 0 — this works because we're on Node.)
`Location` can be relative (`/r2` in my run). Always `new URL(loc, cur).href` before the allowlist check, or you'll validate a relative string.

Replaying the body across a 307/308 hop works only because the SDK always passes a JSON *string* body (`JSON.stringify(message)`); a stream body would be unreplayable. Fine today, but don't 'improve' the hop loop into something that assumes streams.

OAuth discovery and token requests also route through the override, via `createFetchWithInit(opts.fetch, opts.requestInit)` (`shared/transport.js:24-38`). That's the SSRF surface that actually matters (arbitrary issuer/metadata URLs) and it's covered for free.
Reconnects are covered: killing the stream 7 times server-side produced exactly 7 custom-fetch calls. `_scheduleReconnection` routes back through `_startOrAuthSse` at `streamableHttp.js:90`.

`SSEClientTransport` is marked `@deprecated` at `sse.d.ts:50`, and `eventSourceInit.fetch` takes precedence over `opts.fetch` (`sse.js:68`) — if MCPRouter ever exposes `eventSourceInit` to config, a tenant-supplied `fetch` there would bypass the guard. Don't pass `eventSourceInit` through from config.
`FetchLike` gives `url: string | URL` — coerce with `String(url)` before parsing; the streamable path hands you a `URL` object, the eventsource path a string.
